title: Gift reactions say 'A {item}' for every item: 'A Apple', 'A Iron Ore', 'A Turnip Seeds', 'A Asparagus'
repro: Give any villager an Apple/Emerald/Eel/Amethyst (102 item names start with a vowel) or any plural item (Seeds, Greens, Boots: ~188). gift_line() just replaces {item}; ~110 of the 126 lines open 'A {item}' (e.g. gift_lines lines/maple/0 'A {item}! You remembered!', birthday/gideon '...A {item}. I— thank you.', lines/maple/3 'Oh. A {item}.').
fix: In GameState.gift_line add an article step before replacing: replace 'A {item}'/'a {item}' with GameState.with_article(n) -> 'an Apple' / 'some Turnip Seeds' / 'a Carrot' (vowel test on the first letter; names ending in s (not ss) or in a small PLURAL list get 'some'), keeping the capital when the line starts with 'A'. No JSON rewrite needed beyond that; add a check in a gift test that 'Apple' gives 'An Apple'. The fallback lines in town.gd _gift_line ('A %s...') need the same helper.

title: Main story text slips: Coldy spells her name C-O-L-D-I-E, Finn answers a line nobody said, an unclear 'You give him the water'
repro: (1) penguins ch3 beat coldy_join (beats/3/lines/4) branch 1: 'Coldy. C-O-L-D-I-E. That is my real name.' but she is Coldy everywhere (companions, toasts, hint 'Coldy joined'). (2) ch2 beats/5/lines/2 Finn: '...He ran, you said? Then he's still out there.' Nobody told him Tomas ran; the Commander scene only leaves a locket (the 'he ran' footprints are Grandfather Auk, ch3 beats/8). (3) ch2 beats/5/lines/4 'He takes the locket then, and turns toward the water so you won't see his face. You give him the water.' reads as a typo. (4) ch4 beats/1 effects/hint 'You can swim and dive anywhere now. The way to the top is the mountain pad now.' (now twice).
fix: (1) 'Coldy. C-O-L-D-Y. That is my real name.' (2) 'No. Don't. I know where. I knew when he stopped writing. ...But there's no him in it, is there? Just the locket. Then he's still out there. Then he can still come home.' (3) '...so you won't see his face. You give him the quiet, and look at the lake too.' (4) 'You can swim and dive anywhere now. The way to the top is the mountain pad.'

title: The town bell is described three ways: no bell at all, a bell Pip has rung, and a bell missing its clapper
repro: story penguins/0/beats/0/lines/0 '...a bell tower with no bell in it'; talk pip/always/1 'I rang the town bell once. ONE time. Nobody lets me forget it.' (Pip is 9; it has been silent 21 years); hearts pip/fall 'Pip would ring the bell. If there was a bell.' But the quest, Alder ♥6, events ev_bell and the ch4 bell beat all have a bell that only needs a gold clapper.
fix: story ch1 line -> '...a bell tower whose bell hasn't rung in twenty-one years'; talk pip/always/1 -> 'I climbed the bell tower once. ONE time. Nobody lets me forget it.'; hearts pip/fall -> 'Pip would ring the bell. Clapper or no clapper. Pip would ring it with a rock.'

title: Favour letters read 'Could you spare 4 Turnip?' / 'You need 4 Turnip' (no plural); Wren's letter uses US 'neighbor' while the game writes neighbour/colour/favourite
repro: mail.gd line ~131 favour letter: "Could you spare %d %s? I'd pay ◆%d..." with GameState.item_name(want) (singular names: Turnip, Egg, Carrot, Bass) when n is 2-6; the turn-in check at ~243 "You need %d %s (you have %d)." has the same issue. mail.gd line 72 penguin mail_2: 'Dear neighbor, something has been howling...' while Alder's letter (line 96) and the rest of the text use British spelling (neighbour, colour, favourite, fertiliser).
fix: Add a small GameState.plural_name(id, n) (n == 1 -> name; names already ending in s / 'Seeds' / known mass nouns (Wood, Stone, Hay, Fiber, Milk, Honey, Flour, Coal...) unchanged; y -> ies; else + s) and use it in both mail strings. Change 'Dear neighbor' to 'Dear neighbour'.
